definition: Winner-take-all is a computer science concept that has been widely applied in behavior-based robotics as a method of action selection for intelligent agents.
details: Winner-take-all systems work by connecting modules (task-designated areas) in such a way that when one action is performed it stops all other actions from being performed, so only one action is occurring at a time. The name comes from the idea that the "winner" action takes all of the motor system's power.

explainer.lead: Winner-take-all is applied in behaviour-based robotics as a method of action selection for intelligent agents. It matters because it ensures only one action runs at a time.

tiers.eli5: A robot has several jobs it could do, but whichever job wins the contest switches off all the others so it does just one thing at a time.
tiers.practitioner: Modules (task-designated areas) are wired so that performing one action stops all others from being performed. A pitfall is that this exclusivity prevents concurrent actions.
tiers.paperLevel: Winner-take-all systems connect modules such that when one action is performed it stops all other actions, so only one action occurs at a time; the name reflects that the winning action takes all of the motor system's power.

explainer.example: A robot with separate modules for avoiding obstacles and seeking a goal performs only the winning module's action while the others are suppressed.
